subject: Numeracy
title: Where is it?
objectives: Children will follow and give simple directions.
content: Over, under and next to, left and right, and giving directions.
teachingActivities: Use the children’s own bodies and real objects; play games such as hide the toy; teach left and right with a wristband on the right hand and a song; keep directions to two steps; let children give directions to friends.
learnerActivities: Use position words and follow and give simple directions.
assessment: Observe whether each child places an object on, under and next to something and follows a two-step direction.
expectedOutcomes: Places an object on, under and next to.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: giving and following directions

lessons.title: Over, under and next to
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use the words over, under, next to, on and in.
successCriteria: Places a toy over, under and next to a box
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, comparing, shapes, time, graphs and money.
lessons.starter: Put a teddy under a chair and say "The teddy is under the chair."
teacherActivities: Move the teddy over, under, in and next to a box.
Let children place the teddy where you say.
Move their own bodies over and under the bench.
learnerActivities: Children crawl under and step over.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Move the teddy over, under, in and next to a box. Children: Children say each position word.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Where is the teddy?" Children: Child says where it is.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children place the teddy where you say. Children: Child places the teddy.
Step 4. Teacher: Move their own bodies over and under the bench. Children: Children crawl under and step over.

practical.title: Where is the teddy?
steps: Put it where the teacher says.
practical.safety: Keep benches low and crawling areas clear and soft. Supervise closely and never let children climb on furniture.

differentiation.support: Use two position words and move together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give position directions to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is it on the box or in the box?

lessons.conclusion: Put the teddy in a box and say goodnight.
lessons.homeConnection: Play hide the toy at home and say where it is.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use the words over, under, next to, on and in" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Left and right
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will learn left and right using their own hands.
successCriteria: Shows their left and right hands
Follows a left or right instruction
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, comparing, shapes, time, graphs and money.
resources: A ribbon for the right hand
lessons.starter: Put a ribbon on each child’s right hand and say "This is your right hand. The other is your left."
teacherActivities: Show right and left hands and say the words.
Sing a left and right song with actions.
Say "Step to the left" or "Step to the right".
Remove the ribbons and try again.
learnerActivities: Children raise the right and left hand.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show right and left hands and say the words. Children: Children raise the right and left hand.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing a left and right song with actions. Children: Children sing and move.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Step to the left" or "Step to the right". Children: Children step left or right.
Step 4. Teacher: Remove the ribbons and try again. Children: Child tries without ribbons.

practical.title: Left and right moves
practical.safety: Leave plenty of space between children and keep the floor clear. Accept that left and right take time to learn.

differentiation.support: Use the ribbon on the right hand throughout.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to point to something on their left.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wave with your right hand and then your left.
lessons.homeConnection: Play left and right games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "learn left and right using their own hands" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A child with a ribbon on the right hand
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Left foot, right foot, step along.

lessons.title: Giving directions
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will follow and give simple directions around the classroom.
successCriteria: Gives a direction to a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, comparing, shapes, time, graphs and money.
lessons.starter: Say "Walk forward two steps and turn right. What do you find?"
teacherActivities: Give a two-step direction and let a child follow it.
Let the child find the hidden toy.
Let children give directions to friends.
Show a simple map and follow the arrows.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give a two-step direction and let a child follow it. Children: Child follows the direction.
Step 2. Teacher: Let the child find the hidden toy. Children: Child finds the toy.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children give directions to friends. Children: Child gives a direction.
Step 4. Teacher: Show a simple map and follow the arrows. Children: Child follows arrows.

practical.title: Treasure hunt
practical.safety: Keep the route clear and supervised. Check for hazards and use a safe indoor or outdoor space.

differentiation.support: Give one-step directions and walk together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give three-step directions.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Where did you find the toy?

expectedOutcomes: Gives a direction to a friend
lessons.conclusion: Put the cones away and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Give simple directions at home to find a hidden toy.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "follow and give simple directions around the classroom" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Position stories
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use position words in a simple story and in play.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, comparing, shapes, time, graphs and money.
resources: A toy house, toy animals and furniture
lessons.starter: Tell a story about a mouse that goes under the table, over the box and next to the cat.
teacherActivities: Act out the story with toys.
Let children make their own story with toys.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the position words.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Act out the story with toys. Children: Children watch and say the position words.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Where did the mouse go?" Children: Child says where.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children make their own story with toys. Children: Child plays and tells.
Step 4. Teacher: Retell the story together. Children: Children retell with position words.

practical.title: Toy story
practical.safety: Use large toys only and supervise sharing. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Use two or three position words only.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a story with four position words.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What was next to the cat?

lessons.conclusion: Put the toys away and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell position stories with toys at bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use position words in a simple story and in play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 position check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses position words and directions.
successCriteria: Uses over, under and next to
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, comparing, shapes, time, graphs and money.
lessons.starter: Sing the left and right song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: position words, left and right and directions.
At each station ask "Where is it?" and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: position words, left and right and directions. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Where is it?" and watch. Children: Child answers and moves.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Position stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use soft and low equipment only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to give directions to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: uses position words; shows left and right; follows directions; gives directions.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
Uses position words and directions with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep using position words at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses position words and directions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
